title: Preparation of monolayer cultures of primary rat and human islet cells on glass for super-resolution and live cell imaging
protocol: Reconstitute laminin or collagen IV to a concentration of 50 μg/ml in HBSS with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺.
Transfer coverslips to a 24- or 48-well plate using sterile forceps.
Coat each glass coverslip or Fluorodish with the laminin or collagen solution.
Incubate coated coverslips at 37°C for 1-2 hours or overnight in an incubator.
Prepare neuronal culture medium as described and filter sterilize it with a disposable bottle filter (0.22 μm).
Warm up the neuronal medium and trypsin (0.05%) at 37°C.
Collect rat or human islets from Petri dishes into a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge the collected islets for 2 minutes at 110 x g (800 rpm).
Aspirate the supernatant and wash the islets three times with PBS.
Remove PBS and add 300-400 μl of pre-warmed 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA solution.
Pipette up and down very slowly with a micropipette using a 1000 μl tip for about 3 minutes until all islets are dissociated and no longer visible in the solution.
Fill the tube up to 15 ml with pre-warmed neuronal medium.
Centrifuge at 350 x g (1400 rpm) for 6 minutes.
Remove laminin/collagen solution from the coverslips/Fluorodishes.
Wash the coverslips three times with HBSS containing Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺.
Let the coverslips air dry for approximately 5 minutes.
Gently remove supernatant from single islet cells and re-suspend in 3 ml neuronal medium.
Take a few microliters of the cell suspension for counting cells.
Seed cells at 35,000 cells/cm² or approximately 30,000 cells on each laminin or collagen-coated coverslip in a 48-well plate, 60,000 cells on a 24-well plate, or 100,000 cells on a Fluorodish.
Incubate seeded cells for about 5-6 hours.
Slowly add neuronal medium to reach final volume of 500 μl in 48-well plates, 1 ml in 24-well plates, and 2.5 ml in Fluorodishes.
Wait 3-4 days until islet cells fully adhere and spread before proceeding with experiments.
